This is a deliberate product decision perhaps, but it removes user-facing state feedback and the PR description does not mention it; at minimum the removed tests indicate lost coverage of previously supported behavior.

findings.title: isProvisioned derived from promRule.provenance, but GrafanaRuleListItem also accepts an operation prop that is never passed by callers
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem accepts an optional `operation?: RuleOperation` prop and passes it to AlertRuleListItem, but neither caller (GrafanaGroupLoader line 70-77 nor FilterView line 157-162) passes `operation`. Since the ruler-based matching that produced Creating/Deleting operations was removed, the prop is dead code. Additionally, isProvisioned is computed as Boolean(provenance) from the prom rule — the newly added provenance field on GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase. If the Prometheus API does not actually populate provenance on rule DTOs (it's an optional field added in this PR), provisioned rules will incorrectly appear editable/deletable in the list. This needs verification against the backend API contract.

findings.title: Menu test asserts exactly 4 items but Delete is silently missing — test enshrines broken delete flow
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants AlertingRuleDelete permission and folder delete permission in beforeEach, then asserts the menu contains silence, copyLink, duplicate, export and `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`. Given the delete permission is granted, a correct implementation would show 5 items (including Delete). The assertion of exactly 4 items passes only because AlertRuleMenu gates Delete on `canDelete && rulerRule` and rulerRule is undefined in the list view (see AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 165). The test therefore locks in the regression where Delete is unavailable from the list view despite the user having delete permissions. The test should either assert Delete is present (and the component fixed) or explicitly document/verify the intended behavior.

findings.title: Test names say 'Should not render' but mocks grant the permission — assertions are inverted relative to test intent
findings.body: The tests are named 'Should not render Edit button for users with the update permission' and mock useIsRuleEditable to return isEditable: true (i.e., the user HAS update permission), then assert the Edit button is NOT in the document. The test names and the mocked state contradict each other: either the name should be 'without the update permission' (matching RulesTable.test.tsx naming) or the mock should return isEditable: false. As written, the test passes but its name misleads future maintainers about what is being verified. Same issue for the Delete test (line 74) and the cloud rule tests (lines 89, 100).

findings.title: useAllAlertRuleAbilities marked @deprecated but still exported and used; deprecation direction contradicts new hooks
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is marked `@deprecated Use {@link useAllRulerRuleAbilities} instead`, but useAllRulerRuleAbilities takes (rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, groupIdentifier) while useAllAlertRuleAbilities takes a CombinedRule and internally derives the groupIdentifier via groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule. The deprecation message points to a hook with a different, lower-level signature, which is not a drop-in replacement. Meanwhile useAlertRuleAbility (singular, line 179) still uses useAllAlertRuleAbilities and is NOT deprecated, and RuleActionsButtons.V2 still calls useRulerRuleAbility directly. The deprecation is misleading and the migration path is unclear; either provide a proper replacement wrapper or remove the @deprecated tag.

findings.title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules remains after ruler prefetch was removed
findings.body: The comment at lines 81-82 says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded'. The ruler prefetch (alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)) was removed in this PR (see diff), so the comment now describes behavior that no longer exists. The comment should be updated to describe the Prometheus group cache population only.

findings.title: Error handling only covers missing promResponse; a failed Prometheus query with error but no data shows the generic error Alert, but a failed query that returns data=undefined with isLoading=false is conflated with 'no data'
findings.body: The component checks `if (!promResponse)` to show an error Alert, but RTK Query returns `data: undefined` both when the query failed AND potentially during refetching/polling edge cases. The old code checked `!rulerResponse && !promResponse`. More importantly, the query error object (promResponse error from useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery) is never inspected — the component destructures only { data, isLoading }, so an HTTP error (e.g., 403, 500) results in data=undefined and the generic 'Failed to load rules' Alert without the actual error message. The old GrafanaRuleLoader surfaced rulerRuleGroupError/promRuleGroupError via RulerRuleLoadingError. Error detail is lost in the new implementation.
